answers.core: Would be more convenient and also would permit to have signal autocompletion inside the editor more easily if it's handled in core.
answers.workaround:
For now I am using the user_signal API, but it's heavy and need a base class for all my ressources. Look something like this:

```gdscript
class_name Data
extends Resource


func _init():
	var all_properties = get_property_list()
	all_properties = all_properties.filter(func(property): return property["usage"] & PROPERTY_USAGE_SCRIPT_VARIABLE and !(property["usage"] & PROPERTY_USAGE_READ_ONLY) )
	for property in all_properties:
		add_user_signal(property["name"]+"_changed",[])
		
```

```gdscript
class_name TestData
extends Data

@export var test: String = "":
	set(value): 
		test = value
		emit_signal("value_type_changed")

```

```gdscript
extends Node

@export var ressource: TestData

func _ready():
	ressource.connect( "test_changed," self._on_test_changed)

func _on_test_changed():
	$UILabel.text = ressource.test

```

We can see to write it"s heavier than the proposed solution, and we have the risk to forget to implement signal emit in setter.

title: Add and emit <property>_changed signal on GDScript custom ressource properties
